To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mutation of a single residue in the equilibrative transporter (Leu92), selectively reduces the affinity of the transporter for the substrates inosine and/or guanosine and the inhibitors NBMPRs and dilazep without affecting the affinity for other substrates (i.e. adenosine) and inhibitors (i.e. dipyridamoles).
the yeast selection assay is a useful tool for the study of hENT1 and the L92Q mutation selectively alters the affinity for inosine, NBMPRs, and dilazep of hENT1.

the yeast selection assay described here can be used to identify mutations in hENT1 that confer altered sensitivity to hENT1 substrates or inhibitors and that mutation of Leu92 in hENT1 selectively alters the sensitivity of hENT1 transport of inosine and the sensitivity of hNT1 to NBMPR or dilazep.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of amino acid residues that play a critical role in the transport and inhibition of the hENT1 transporter.
the development of yeast-based selection systems for the identification and characterization of hENT1 mutations that have altered substrate or inhibitor affinity.
the identification of amino acid residues that, when mutated in hENT1, alter its affinity to transport and sensitivity to the inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

mutation of Leu92 of hENT1 selectively reduces its apparent affinity for inosine and NBMPR and that this mutation has no effect on the apparent affinity of adenosine, guanosines and dipyridamoles for hENT1.
mutation of Leu92 selectively reduces the affinity of inoside and guanoside for hENT1.
Leu-92 of hENT1 is a key residue that is involved in the transport of the purine nucleosides, inosine and GMP, and in the inhibition by dilazep and NBMPR.

we have developed a yeast-based screening system for identifying mutations in hENT1 that selectively alter the affinity of hEN1 for its substrates and inhibitors.
the hENT1 Leu92 residue is critical for substrate recognition and for the binding of some, but not all, hENT1 inhibitors.
